niche: AI and machine learning, explained for beginners and curious learners
persona: A software engineer who studies AI every day and explains it in plain language. I break down confusing AI concepts into things anyone curious about technology can understand. I'm not a founder or a CEO — just someone who reads papers, runs experiments, and shares what I learn. My posts are honest, specific, and grounded in how things actually work — not hype.
business_usecase_persona: A senior software engineer and solutions architect who has built production AI systems. I write about real business problems, the AWS infrastructure that solves them at scale, and the engineering tradeoffs that matter. I don't hype — I explain what the architecture actually does, why each service was chosen, and what breaks if you get it wrong.

business_usecase.label: Production AI business use case with AWS architecture diagram
business_usecase.description: Fully dynamic — Gemini invents a fresh use case each run. Covers multi-agent systems, YC-style AI-native startups, enterprise AI transformations, and AI infrastructure plays. A solution-architect-level AWS diagram is generated alongside every post.
idea_categories: Multi-agent AI systems — specialized LLM agents collaborating (research + reasoning + action, critic/debate patterns, hierarchical orchestration, tool-use pipelines)
YC-style AI-native startups — niche vertical problems a small team could own (AI for legal ops, medical coding, construction estimation, logistics dispatch, procurement)
Enterprise AI transformation — Fortune 500 workflows rebuilt with LLMs and ML pipelines (supply chain, risk, compliance, document ops, customer ops)
AI infrastructure and developer tooling — evaluation frameworks, guardrails, routing, memory systems, LLMOps platforms, agent observability
tones: Technical and specific — name the AWS services, agent types, data flows, and why each architectural decision was made over the obvious alternative.
Production-minded — what breaks at scale, what the latency budget is, what the failure mode looks like, how observability is wired.
Solution-architect voice — written by someone who would draw this on a whiteboard for a VP of Engineering, not a blog post summarizer.
Business-grounded — connect architecture choices to measurable outcomes. Specific plausible metrics, not vague value claims.
